title: Verifier-Guided Task Decomposition for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
research_question: Can integrating a lightweight verifier that scores decomposition soundness and inter-agent dependency consistency improve task success and reduce wasted agent calls in multi-agent LLM workflows compared with standard planner-only orchestration?
hypothesis: A verifier-guided orchestration loop that checks decomposition quality before execution and triggers selective re-planning when dependencies are inconsistent will yield higher end-to-end success rates and lower orchestration cost than planner-only or escalation-only multi-agent workflows.
motivation: The knowledge base shows recent rejected ideas clustered around uncertainty averaging and escalation policies for agentic workflows, suggesting saturation in those directions. At the same time, the self-adaptive systems literature in the KB highlights an underexplored issue: systems fail when they commit too early to a single model or plan and need explicit analysis-time mechanisms to detect poor choices before costly execution. Translating that gap to multi-agent LLM workflows suggests a more novel direction: not averaging agents or escalating after failure, but verifying task decomposition quality and dependency consistency before and during execution. This could address a practical bottleneck in agent orchestration—expensive downstream errors caused by flawed decomposition—while staying distinct from already rejected ideas.
